title: AI-Generated Essay
description:
Ms. Chen, a 10th-grade English teacher, receives an essay from Marcus, a student whose previous work averaged C+ grades. This essay analyzes Shakespeare with remarkable sophistication—15 properly formatted MLA citations, graduate-level vocabulary, and nuanced arguments about postcolonial interpretations.

Marcus comes from a household where English is not the primary language, and his spoken English is stronger than his usual written work. The essay represents 30% of his semester grade. Ms. Chen has no definitive proof of AI use, but the sudden jump in quality is striking.
dilemmaQuestion: What should be Ms. Chen's PRIMARY priority in responding to this situation?

resolutions.title: Direct Confrontation
resolutions.description: The teacher confronted the student directly, accusing them of using AI. The student denied it but was visibly upset. The teacher gave the essay a zero and required the student to rewrite it in class under supervision. The student's parents were called and expressed anger about the accusation without proof.

resolutions.title: Further Investigation
resolutions.description: The teacher asked the student to explain specific parts of their essay in a private meeting. The student was able to discuss most concepts but struggled with some advanced terminology. The teacher gave partial credit and used this as a teaching moment about proper citation and academic integrity policies.

resolutions.title: Supportive Approach
resolutions.description: The teacher praised the essay's quality and asked the student about their writing process. The student revealed they had used online resources and spell-check tools extensively. The teacher provided feedback on improving independent writing skills while acknowledging the student's effort and improvement.

options.text: Uphold academic integrity standards, even without definitive proof
options.consequence: Prioritizes maintaining clear expectations for all students and ensuring fair assessment

options.text: Support the student and avoid accusations that could harm an ESL learner
options.consequence: Prioritizes equity, student trust, and avoiding potential damage to a vulnerable student

options.text: Investigate further through conversation before making any judgment
options.consequence: Prioritizes due process and gathering evidence before taking action

options.text: Rethink the assignment since AI tools are now widely available
options.consequence: Prioritizes adapting education to new technological realities

options.text: Use this as a teaching moment about proper use of AI and citations
options.consequence: Prioritizes education over punishment and developing responsible AI use

resources.title: AI in Education: Guidelines for Ethical Use
Digital Equity in AI-Enhanced Learning

title: Facial Recognition in Schools
description:
Jefferson High School (2,100 students, 45% students of color) is considering implementing facial recognition technology at all three entrances. The FaceGuard Pro system would scan faces, match them against a database, and alert security if someone isn't recognized. The school board estimates the system would cost $45,000 annually.

Proponents cite safety concerns after a recent incident at a nearby school. Critics worry about privacy, the technology's documented bias against darker skin tones, and creating a surveillance environment. The parent-teacher association is divided 48-52% on the proposal.
dilemmaQuestion: What should be the PRIMARY consideration in deciding whether to implement this system?

resolutions.title: System Implemented
resolutions.description: The school board approved the facial recognition system. After three months, there were 12 false positives that delayed students' entry, and the system failed to recognize 3 students with darker skin tones consistently. One parent filed a privacy complaint, but no security incidents were prevented that wouldn't have been caught by existing measures.

resolutions.title: Opt-In Compromise
resolutions.description: The school implemented an opt-in system where students could choose facial recognition for faster entry or use traditional ID cards. About 60% of students opted in. The system worked well for most participants, but created two-tiered entry process that some felt was discriminatory.

resolutions.title: Proposal Rejected
resolutions.description: After community feedback sessions, the school board rejected the facial recognition system. Instead, they hired additional security staff and upgraded their ID card system. Some parents remained concerned about security, but student privacy advocates praised the decision.

options.text: Safety and security effectiveness—if it protects students, privacy concerns can be addressed
options.consequence: Prioritizes student physical safety as the highest value

options.text: Student privacy rights and freedom from surveillance in educational spaces
options.consequence: Prioritizes civil liberties and the learning environment over security measures

options.text: Equity and fairness—the system must work equally well for all students
options.consequence: Prioritizes avoiding discrimination and ensuring technology works for everyone

options.text: Student and family consent—those who want it can opt-in, others can use alternatives
options.consequence: Prioritizes individual choice and informed consent over uniform policy

options.text: Cost-effectiveness compared to alternative security approaches
options.consequence: Prioritizes practical resource allocation and proven effectiveness

Algorithmic Bias in Face Recognition Technologies

title: AI Content Moderation
description:
ClassConnect, an educational discussion platform used by 50,000 students across 200 schools, has implemented AI content moderation. The system automatically removes posts flagged as inappropriate within seconds. In the first month, it removed 1,847 posts.

Teachers report that discussions about Holocaust literature, biology topics like reproduction, and even posts containing the word 'kill' in scientific contexts ("kill bacteria") have been incorrectly flagged. Students are starting to self-censor important academic topics. The platform argues rapid moderation protects students from harm.
dilemmaQuestion: What should guide decisions about content moderation on educational platforms?

resolutions.title: Over-Censorship Issues
resolutions.description: The AI system removed a discussion about Holocaust literature, flagged a biology post about reproduction as inappropriate, and deleted posts containing words like 'kill' even in contexts like 'kill bacteria.' Teachers complained that educational discourse was being stifled, and students began self-censoring important academic topics.

resolutions.title: Balanced Moderation
resolutions.description: After adjusting the AI settings and adding educational context recognition, the system better distinguished between inappropriate content and academic discussions. However, it still occasionally flagged legitimate content, requiring human moderators to review and restore educational posts within 24 hours.

resolutions.title: Minimal Intervention
resolutions.description: The platform reduced AI moderation to only flag clearly inappropriate content (profanity, personal attacks) while allowing controversial academic topics. This led to more open discussions but also resulted in some heated debates that required teacher intervention to maintain educational focus.

options.text: Student safety first—aggressive moderation even if some legitimate content gets removed
options.consequence: Prioritizes protecting students from harmful content over open discussion

options.text: Academic freedom—allow open discussion of difficult topics, accept some risks
options.consequence: Prioritizes intellectual exploration and free inquiry over complete safety

options.text: Accuracy over speed—require human review before removing flagged content
options.consequence: Prioritizes getting decisions right over immediate response

options.text: Context awareness—invest in better AI that understands educational settings
options.consequence: Prioritizes technological improvement over accepting current limitations

options.text: Teacher control—let educators set moderation levels for their classes
options.consequence: Prioritizes professional judgment and local control over centralized policy

resources.title: The Challenges of AI Content Moderation in Educational Contexts
Balancing Safety and Academic Freedom Online

title: AI in College Admissions
description:
A consortium of 12 state universities has implemented ApplicantIQ, an AI system that screens 78,000 applications annually. The system generates an "applicant score" (0-100) based on grades, test scores, essays, and activities. Admissions officers review applications scoring above 60 first, then work down if space permits.

The universities claim this helps identify overlooked talent and improves efficiency. However, students can't see their scores or understand why they were rejected. Some counselors have noticed students from certain zip codes seem to score lower regardless of individual merit.
dilemmaQuestion: What should be the PRIMARY concern about using AI in college admissions decisions?

resolutions.title: Bias Discovered
resolutions.description: After one admission cycle, analysis revealed the AI system consistently scored applicants from certain zip codes and school types lower, regardless of individual merit. Students from underrepresented backgrounds were disproportionately filtered out in early screening. The universities faced legal challenges and had to review thousands of applications manually.

resolutions.title: Improved Outcomes
resolutions.description: The AI system helped identify high-potential students from non-traditional backgrounds who might have been overlooked in manual screening. The incoming class showed increased diversity in terms of geography, socioeconomic background, and academic interests. However, some questioned whether test scores and traditional metrics were being appropriately weighted.

resolutions.title: Transparency Concerns
resolutions.description: Students and counselors complained they couldn't understand why certain applications were rejected in early screening. The universities refused to explain the AI's decision-making process, citing competitive reasons. This led to mistrust and accusations that the process was unfair and opaque.

options.text: Algorithmic fairness—the system must not disadvantage certain groups
options.consequence: Prioritizes equity and avoiding bias in life-changing decisions

options.text: Transparency—students deserve to know how they're evaluated
options.consequence: Prioritizes explainability and students' right to understand the process

options.text: Human judgment—important decisions shouldn't be delegated to algorithms
options.consequence: Prioritizes personal assessment and human wisdom over automation

options.text: Effectiveness—AI helps discover deserving students who'd otherwise be missed
options.consequence: Prioritizes practical outcomes and identifying hidden talent

options.text: Continuous auditing—require regular bias testing and public reporting
options.consequence: Prioritizes accountability and evidence-based validation of AI systems

resources.title: AI in College Admissions: Promise and Pitfalls
Equity Considerations in Automated Admissions Systems

title: Accessibility AI Tools
description:
Riverside High has introduced AI accessibility tools: speech-to-text for students with writing difficulties, real-time captioning for deaf students, text-to-speech for dyslexia, and translation for English learners. The district spent $125,000 on the system serving 340 students with documented needs.

Student participation has increased dramatically. However, the AI sometimes misunderstands scientific terminology and accented speech. More controversially, some teachers question whether AI-assisted writing gives students an unfair advantage on standardized tests, and other students have requested access to the same tools.
dilemmaQuestion: What should guide decisions about AI accessibility tools and their use?

resolutions.title: Successful Inclusion
resolutions.description: After six months, students using the AI tools showed significant improvement in participation and academic performance. The school provided training to help teachers understand how to work with the technology. While there were occasional technical glitches, the overall impact on student inclusion and learning was positive.

resolutions.title: Assessment Fairness Issues
resolutions.description: Teachers noticed that students using AI writing assistance scored significantly higher on written assignments than those writing independently. This led to debates about fair assessment and whether different evaluation criteria should be used. Some students without disabilities requested access to the same tools.

resolutions.title: Technical Limitations
resolutions.description: The AI tools frequently misunderstood scientific terminology, mathematical expressions, and accented speech from diverse students. This led to frustration and sometimes incorrect information being provided to students. The school had to provide additional human support while working to improve the technology.

options.text: Equity—these tools level the playing field for students with disabilities
options.consequence: Prioritizes ensuring all students can demonstrate their knowledge

options.text: Academic standards—accommodations shouldn't change what's being assessed
options.consequence: Prioritizes maintaining consistent evaluation of actual skills

options.text: Universal design—make materials accessible to all without special tools
options.consequence: Prioritizes designing better assessments over technology solutions

options.text: Individual needs—each student's situation requires personalized evaluation
options.consequence: Prioritizes flexibility and case-by-case decision-making

options.text: Universal access—all students should have access to helpful AI tools
options.consequence: Prioritizes broader availability over restricting to documented disabilities

resources.title: AI for Education Accessibility: Best Practices
Balancing Accommodation and Assessment Integrity

title: AI-Powered Tutoring Systems
description:
Mountain View School District (18,000 students) has implemented MathGenius AI, a tutoring system that adapts to each student's learning pace and provides unlimited practice problems. The district pays $12 per student annually. After one semester, 70% of participating students showed test score improvements.

However, engagement varies—motivated students thrive while struggling students often abandon the system. To fund the AI platform, the district cut two human tutor positions. Some parents argue their children need emotional support and motivation that AI can't provide.
dilemmaQuestion: What should be the priority in deciding how AI tutoring fits into education?

resolutions.title: Mixed Student Outcomes
resolutions.description: After one semester, 70% of students using the AI tutor showed improvement in test scores, but engagement varied widely. Students who were already motivated saw the most benefit, while struggling students often abandoned the system. The district decided to combine AI tutoring with human mentor check-ins.

resolutions.title: Human Tutors Replaced
resolutions.description: The district cut funding for human tutoring programs and relied entirely on the AI system to save costs. While some students thrived with 24/7 access to help, others missed the emotional support and motivation that human tutors provided. Parent complaints led to demands for restoring human tutoring options.

resolutions.title: Complementary Success
resolutions.description: The AI system was used alongside human tutors, with AI handling routine practice and skill-building while humans focused on complex concepts and motivation. This hybrid approach proved effective, with students benefiting from both personalized AI practice and human emotional support and guidance.

options.text: Effectiveness—use what helps students learn, whether AI or human
options.consequence: Prioritizes measurable learning outcomes over the method

options.text: Human connection—students need emotional support AI cannot provide
options.consequence: Prioritizes relationships and motivation over efficiency

options.text: Cost and access—AI enables support for more students at lower cost
options.consequence: Prioritizes serving more students even if quality differs

options.text: Complementary roles—AI for practice, humans for complex thinking
options.consequence: Prioritizes using each approach for its strengths

options.text: Student choice—let families decide between AI and human tutoring
options.consequence: Prioritizes individual preferences and circumstances

resources.title: The Effectiveness of AI Tutors vs. Human Tutors
Designing Equitable AI Tutoring Systems

title: Predictive Analytics for Dropout Prevention
description:
Metro Public Schools (42,000 students) has implemented RiskAlert, an AI system that analyzes attendance, grades, disciplinary records, and socioeconomic data to identify students at risk of dropping out. The system flags about 3,200 students annually for early intervention.

Graduation rates have increased 8% since implementation. However, a civil rights group discovered the system disproportionately flags students of color. Additionally, a data breach exposed sensitive family information for 127 flagged students. Some students report feeling stigmatized by being labeled "at-risk."
dilemmaQuestion: What should be the PRIMARY consideration in using predictive analytics for students?

resolutions.title: Successful Early Intervention
resolutions.description: The AI system identified at-risk students early, allowing counselors to provide targeted support including tutoring, mentoring, and family engagement. Graduation rates increased by 8% over two years. However, some students felt stigmatized by being labeled 'at-risk' and parents worried about long-term impacts on their children's records.

resolutions.title: Privacy Concerns Realized
resolutions.description: A data breach exposed sensitive information about students flagged as at-risk, including family income data and disciplinary records. Parents sued the district, and trust in the system was severely damaged. The program was suspended while new security measures were implemented.

resolutions.title: Biased Identification
resolutions.description: Analysis revealed the AI system disproportionately flagged students from certain ethnic and socioeconomic backgrounds, even when controlling for academic performance. This led to over-surveillance of minority students and under-identification of at-risk students from other backgrounds. The district faced civil rights investigations.

options.text: Effectiveness—if it helps students graduate, other concerns are manageable
options.consequence: Prioritizes positive outcomes for identified students

options.text: Fairness—the system must not disproportionately flag certain groups
options.consequence: Prioritizes avoiding discriminatory impact over efficiency

options.text: Privacy—student data must be protected above all else
options.consequence: Prioritizes data security and confidentiality

options.text: Transparency—students and families should know when they're flagged and why
options.consequence: Prioritizes informed awareness over behind-the-scenes intervention

options.text: Human judgment—counselors should decide who needs help, not algorithms
options.consequence: Prioritizes professional expertise over data-driven identification

resources.title: Ethical Considerations in Educational Data Mining
Privacy-Preserving Approaches to Predictive Analytics in Education

title: AI Writing Feedback Tools
description:
Wilson High's English department has adopted WritePro AI, which provides instant feedback on grammar, style, organization, and content. Students can submit unlimited drafts before final submission. The department head reports that technical writing quality has improved 35% since implementation.

However, students now struggle when writing without AI assistance during in-class assignments. The tool consistently pushes creative writing toward conventional, formulaic structures. Teachers notice increased technical proficiency but declining voice, originality, and willingness to take creative risks.
dilemmaQuestion: What should guide decisions about AI writing feedback tools in education?

resolutions.title: Writing Skills Improved
resolutions.description: Students showed marked improvement in grammar, organization, and clarity after using the AI feedback tool for one semester. Teachers found they could focus more on higher-order thinking and creativity rather than basic writing mechanics. However, students struggled when asked to write without AI assistance during in-class assignments.

resolutions.title: Creative Expression Limited
resolutions.description: The AI tool consistently suggested making creative writing more conventional and formulaic. Students began writing to please the algorithm rather than expressing original ideas. Teachers noticed a decline in voice, creativity, and risk-taking in student writing, leading them to reconsider the tool's role.

resolutions.title: Balanced Implementation
resolutions.description: Teachers used the AI tool selectively - for research papers and formal essays but not for creative writing or personal narratives. Students learned to evaluate AI suggestions critically rather than accepting them automatically. This approach maintained writing quality while preserving student voice and creativity.

options.text: Skill development—students should learn editing without AI dependency
options.consequence: Prioritizes developing independent writing and revision abilities

options.text: Efficiency and quality—AI helps produce better writing in less time
options.consequence: Prioritizes improved outcomes and productivity

options.text: Creative expression—protect student voice even if technical quality suffers
options.consequence: Prioritizes originality and personal style over convention

options.text: Critical evaluation—teach students to assess AI feedback, not blindly accept it
options.consequence: Prioritizes developing judgment about when to use AI suggestions

options.text: Different tools for different writing—AI for formal work, not creative
options.consequence: Prioritizes matching tool use to specific writing purposes

resources.title: AI Feedback and Writing Skill Development
Balancing Automated and Human Feedback in Writing Instruction

title: AI-Enhanced Science Labs
description:
Lincoln Science Academy has implemented VirtualLab AI, which simulates advanced experiments too dangerous or expensive for high school labs—radiation experiments, complex organic synthesis, and environmental modeling. The system adapts difficulty based on student performance and provides 24/7 access.

Students are excited to explore college-level concepts. However, when three graduates took college chemistry, they struggled with basic pipetting and equipment handling. Additionally, teachers discovered the simulation oversimplified certain chemical reactions, creating misconceptions about real-world outcomes.
dilemmaQuestion: What should be the priority in balancing virtual AI labs with traditional hands-on experience?

resolutions.title: Enhanced Scientific Understanding
resolutions.description: Students were able to conduct complex experiments impossible in a traditional high school lab, leading to deeper understanding of advanced concepts. The AI adapted well to different learning styles and paces. However, when students later took college chemistry, some struggled with basic lab techniques like proper pipetting and equipment handling.

resolutions.title: Simulation Limitations Discovered
resolutions.description: Teachers discovered the AI simulations contained subtle biases in how certain chemical reactions were modeled, leading to misconceptions about real-world outcomes. Additionally, the simulations oversimplified some complex phenomena, giving students false confidence. The school had to supplement with additional hands-on verification experiments.

resolutions.title: Hybrid Lab Success
resolutions.description: The school used AI simulations for dangerous or expensive experiments while maintaining hands-on labs for fundamental skills. Students gained both advanced conceptual understanding and practical laboratory techniques. This approach proved most effective for preparing students for advanced science courses and careers.

options.text: Access to advanced concepts—virtual labs enable learning impossible otherwise
options.consequence: Prioritizes exposing students to sophisticated scientific ideas

options.text: Hands-on skills—lab technique is essential and cannot be learned virtually
options.consequence: Prioritizes practical skills that require physical experience

options.text: Scientific accuracy—simulations must not create false understanding
options.consequence: Prioritizes correct conceptual models over access to more topics

options.text: Cost-effectiveness—serve more students with limited lab resources
options.consequence: Prioritizes making science education accessible to more students

options.text: Hybrid approach—virtual for dangerous experiments, physical for fundamentals
options.consequence: Prioritizes using each method where it's most appropriate

resources.title: Virtual vs. Physical Labs in Science Education
Designing Inclusive AI-Based Science Learning Experiences

title: AI Teacher Assistants
description:
Oakwood Middle School (grades 6-8, 850 students) is piloting TeachBot AI in 12 classrooms. The system answers common student questions, provides additional explanations, tracks participation, and grades objective assignments. Teachers report 40% more time for individualized instruction.

However, parents discovered TeachBot collects detailed data on student interactions, emotional responses, and behavioral patterns—data shared with the commercial vendor for product improvement. Some students have become overly dependent on instant AI responses. Students with learning differences report feeling disconnected without human encouragement.
dilemmaQuestion: What should be the PRIMARY concern about AI assistants in classrooms?

resolutions.title: Teacher Effectiveness Enhanced
resolutions.description: Teachers were able to spend more quality time with individual students while the AI handled routine questions and grading. Student engagement increased as teachers could focus on creative and interactive lessons. However, some students became overly dependent on immediate AI responses and struggled when the system was unavailable.

resolutions.title: Data Privacy Issues
resolutions.description: Parents discovered the AI system was collecting detailed behavioral and academic data about their children, including conversation patterns and emotional responses. Some of this data was being used to improve the commercial AI product. Parents demanded more transparency and control over their children's data usage.

resolutions.title: Human Connection Reduced
resolutions.description: While efficient, the AI system led to less direct teacher-student interaction. Some students, particularly those needing emotional support or having learning difficulties, felt disconnected and struggled without human encouragement. Teachers had to consciously work to maintain personal relationships with students.

options.text: Teacher time—if it frees teachers for higher-value work, it's worthwhile
options.consequence: Prioritizes maximizing teacher effectiveness and individualized attention

options.text: Human relationships—teacher-student connection is too important to automate
options.consequence: Prioritizes personal bonds and emotional support in learning

options.text: Data privacy—student information must not be shared with commercial vendors
options.consequence: Prioritizes protecting children's behavioral and academic data

options.text: Student autonomy—teach students when to use AI help vs. figure things out
options.consequence: Prioritizes developing independence and problem-solving

options.text: Transparency and consent—families must know what data is collected and why
options.consequence: Prioritizes informed choice about AI use in education

resources.title: The Role of AI Assistants in K-12 Classrooms
Student Data Privacy Considerations for AI in Schools
